open_issues: Post-deadline, pre-draft trades (in router_2025.POST_DEADLINE_CHANGES): #23 IND at the deadline, traded to NOP on 2025-06-17 (NBA_IND_NOP); #16 ORL at the deadline, traded to MEM in the Bane trade on 2025-06-15 (NBA_BANE). Rules give the deadline holder.

OKC/LAC/HOU/PHX/BKN network: the JSON's two rank pools are exact only when OKC's best target is the LAC pick. The full logic, with all branches, is in router_2025.py: OKC takes the more favorable of LAC's and HOU's picks (HOU not eligible if 1-10) if it beats its own, and the team it swapped with gets OKC's pick; HOU then swaps whichever pick it holds (its own, or OKC's) with BKN for the PHX pick if that is better. The ordering, eligibility and choice rules are marked ASSUMPTION in the module.
MIL: JSON rule 'to BKN' is approximate; router_2025.py routes it exactly (NOP if 1-4, BKN if 5-30).

Realized holders follow NBA.com's selecting team. Several trades were agreed before the draft but completed afterward: #10 HOU->PHX (Durant trade), #22 ATL->BKN (Porzingis three-team trade), #29 PHX->CHA; HR's updated order lists PHX at #10 and BKN at #22. Recorded holders HOU and ATL, which match the deadline rules.
Draft-night trades (not mismatches): #11 POR<->#16 MEM, #13 ATL<->#23 NOP, #18 WAS<->#21 UTA, #24 OKC->SAC.

HR_aug24 appears to have been updated after publication (it lists IND->NOP and ORL->MEM, which only happened in June 2025, and CHA->SAC from the Feb 2025 Fox trade); used only for original protection wording, which agrees with HR_mar25.
No 2025 first-round picks forfeited per sources checked (NYK/PHI forfeitures in this period were second-rounders).
The executable router router_2025.py is authoritative where the rank grammar can't express the terms; see its ASSUMPTIONS list.
